And: I have given you power (Luke 10), etc. Went to, etc. He went to the chief priests: and after he went out, Satan entered into him. Here night shows knowledge to night. Every animal is joined to its like (Matt. 28). Mary runs to the apostles that day may utter speech to day; Judas to the Jews, that night may show knowledge to night.
14.11: 14.11 And he sought how he might, etc. JEROME. He promises to betray him, as his Master had said before: To you I will give all this power. BEDE. Many today shudder at the crime of Judas and yet do not beware, etc., up to so that, the witnesses being removed, they may change truth by lie, virtue by crime.
14.12: 14.12 And on the first day of the unleavened bread. THE SAME. On the fourteenth moon, when the lamb was killed toward evening, the leaven having been cast away, etc., up to he hallowed the beginning of the immolation itself, that is, of his own passion. ISIDORE. The unleavened bread, which is our redemption, is eaten with bitterness. For the bitterness is the passion of the Lord.
14.13: 14.13 Go into the city. BEDE. It is a sign of divine foreknowledge, etc., up to and the baptism of the life-giving fountain is consecrated for the taking away of the crimes of the world. JEROME. The city is the Church, which is girded with the wall of faith: the man who meets them is the primitive people, the pitcher of water the law of the letter. A man carrying a pitcher of water. BEDE. Purposely both the water-carrier and the house of the Lord are left unnamed, that the means may be signified to be given to all who wish to celebrate the true Pasch, that is, to be imbued with the sacraments of Christ, and who seek to receive him into the lodging of their mind. Follow him. JEROME. Who leads to the height where is the refreshment of Christ, hence Rahab commands the spies not to go by the low places but by the high.
14.15: 14.15 A large dining room. THE SAME. The great Church, which tells the name of the Lord, furnished with the variety of virtues and tongues, hence: Surrounded with variety (Ps. 44) of virtues, in which the Pasch is prepared for the Lord. The master of the house is Peter the apostle, to whom the Lord entrusted his house: that there be one faith under one shepherd. BEDE. The dining room is the spiritual law, which, going out from the narrowness of the letter, receives the Savior in a lofty place, etc., up to because it knows that all the sacraments of the Pasch and the other decrees of the law are his sacraments.
14.17: 14.17 And when evening was come. JEROME. The evening of the day indicates the evening of the world. For about the eleventh hour the last come: who receive first the penny of eternal life: because before the cross Abraham was in hell, and after the cross the thief in paradise.
14.18: 14.18 Amen I say, etc. As he had foretold of the passion, so he foretells of the betrayer, giving place for repentance, so that when he understood that his thoughts were foreknown by God, he might repent of his deed. Yet he does not designate him by name, lest, openly convicted, he become more shameless. He casts the crime into the number: that the guilty may do penance. One of you. While the falsehood is accused, the truth is proved and fulfilled. He who ate my bread has greatly supplanted me (Ps. 40). All are touched so that harmony may be made on the harp. All the strings, well strung, respond with one voice: Is it I, Lord? One, slack and affected by love of money, said: Is it I, Rabbi?
14.19: 14.19 To be sorrowful. Like the eleven, because they had thought no evil against the Lord: but they trust their Master more than themselves, and fearing their own frailty, sad, they ask about a sin of which they had no consciousness.
14.20: 14.20 One of the twelve. JEROME. The wolf separates apart the sheep he desires. The sheep that goes out from the fold is open to the bites of the wolf. Who dips. BEDE. Wonderful patience of the Lord. He first said: One of you shall betray me; the betrayer persists in evil. He rebukes more openly: and yet he is not properly designated. Judas, while the others were saddened and withdrawing their hands from the food, with the rashness and shamelessness with which he betrays the Lord, even puts his hand with the Master into the dish, so that by boldness he might feign a good conscience.
14.21: 14.21 But woe. THE SAME. Woe forever to that man who approaches the Lord's table unworthily, etc., up to the punishment is foretold so that he who is not conquered by shame may be corrected by fear.
14.22: 14.22 As they were eating. THE SAME. The old Passover, which was celebrated in commemoration of the liberation of God's people from Egypt, having ended, etc., up to and therefore to be raised more swiftly from death. He took. JEROME. Prefiguring his body in bread, etc., up to the enemies are destroyed, which are the mysteries of the Church of Christ. BEDE. The bread that strengthens the heart of man, etc., up to or that we are saved without his passion.
14.23: 14.23 Thanks. He gave thanks and blessed, being now close to the passion, he who takes on the punishment of another's iniquity, who had done nothing worthy of the passion, to show how calmly each one ought to endure the scourges of his own fault. They all drank. JEROME. Blessed drunkenness, salutary fullness, etc., up to for the blood of the New Testament, which is shed for many, does not cleanse all.
14.25: 14.25 I will not drink. THE SAME. Here he changes the sacrifice, but does not change the time; so that we may never celebrate the supper of Jesus before the fourteenth moon. He who makes the resurrection on the fourteenth makes the Lord's supper on the eleventh, which has never been found in either the New or the Old Testament. The vine. BEDE. The vine or vineyard of the Lord is the Synagogue, etc., up to concerning the salvation of that same people, regenerated in baptism, I shall be filled with new joy together with you.
14.26: 14.26 And when they had sung a hymn. THE SAME. It can be understood as the hymn which, according to John, he sang while giving thanks to the Father, etc., up to and the gifts of the Holy Spirit with which we are anointed in the heart, we ought to ascend. To the Mount of Olives. JEROME. Jesus is seized on the Mount of Olives, and from there he ascends to heaven, so that we may know that we ascend to heaven from the place where we keep watch, and pray, and are bound, and do not resist on earth. You will all be scandalized. BEDE. He foretells what they are going to suffer, so that when they have suffered it they may not despair, but repent.
14.27: 14.27 This night. Those who are drunk are drunk by night (1 Thess. 5), and those who are scandalized are scandalized by night, that is, with the mind darkened. JEROME. All fall, but not all lie fallen. Shall he that sleeps not add to rise again? (Zach. 13). To fall is of the flesh; to lie fallen is of the devil. I will strike the shepherd. Strike the shepherd. The prophet asks for the Lord's passion; the Father answers: I will strike the shepherd. By the prayers of the saints the Son is sent by the Father, that is, he is incarnate and struck and suffers; the sheep are scattered when the shepherd is taken. The resurrection is promised so that hope may not be extinguished.
14.29: 14.29 But Peter. THE SAME. A bird without feathers strives to fly aloft; but the body weighs down the soul, so that through fear of human death the fear of the Lord is overcome.
14.30: 14.30 Twice the cock crows. BEDE. Others simply say: Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times, etc., up to as also that: He who has looked on a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart (Matt. 5). JEROME. The cock crows; Peter denies three times, etc., up to and he washed the stains of the threefold denial with tears.
14.32: 14.32 Gethsemani. THE SAME. That is, the valley of the fat ones, where fat bulls besieged him and many calves surrounded him. Sit you here. ISIDORE. Those who are separated in the passion are separated in prayer, because he prays, they sleep, weighed down by fatness of heart. While I pray. BEDE. When the Lord prays on the mountain, etc., up to whence: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death. And greater love than this no man has, that a man lay down his life for his friends (Phil. 2; John 15).
14.33: 14.33 And he began to fear. JEROME. We are taught to fear and be sad before the judgment of death, we who cannot say of ourselves, but only through him: The prince of this world comes, and in me he has nothing (John 14).
14.34: 14.34 My soul is sorrowful, etc. BEDE. He is not sorrowful because of death, etc., up to but from the sleep of unbelief and the torpor of the mind.
14.35: 14.35 And he prayed. THE SAME. This voice is the sound of our weakness, etc., up to but because it will not be otherwise, Not what I will, but what you will. JEROME. This is against the Eutychians, who say there is only one operation and one will in Christ; but here he shows the human will, which through the weakness of the flesh refuses the passion, and the divine will, which is ready to accomplish the dispensation.
14.36: 14.36 But not what. JEROME. To the very end he does not cease to teach us to obey our fathers, and to put their will before our own will.
14.37: 14.37 And he said to Peter, etc. He who had said: Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you; even if all shall be scandalized, yet not I (Matt. 26); now by the greatness of his sorrow he cannot overcome sleep.
14.38: 14.38 That you enter not. He does not say, that you be not tempted, but that you enter not into temptation, that is, that the temptation not overcome you, nor hold you within its snares. JEROME. He who neglects to pray enters into temptation. Three times the disciples sleep; three times the Lord, praying, wakes them. The threefold sleep signifies the three dead whom the Lord raised: the first in the house, the second at the tomb, the third out of the tomb. The Lord's threefold watch teaches us to have three persons in praying, and to ask pardon for things past, present, and future. But the flesh is weak. BEDE. For the flesh by its weight always drags downward.
14.42: 14.42 Rise up. After he had prayed the third time, he taught that the fear of the apostles was to be corrected by repentance; he goes on to the passion in security, saying: Rise up, let us go. As if to say: Let them not find us fearful, but let us go of our own accord to meet them, so that those who are to suffer may see joy and confidence.
14.44: 14.44 A sign. JEROME. He gives the sign of a kiss with the devil's poison, as Cain offered a deceitful and rejected sacrifice, whence they put wine with vinegar on the cross.
14.45: 14.45 Rabbi. BEDE. With shameless and wicked confidence he calls him master, etc., up to he also fulfills that: With those who hated peace (Ps. 119), etc.
14.47: 14.47 One. THE SAME. Peter, according to John, with the same ardor of mind as in the rest. For he knew that Phinees, by punishing sacrilegious men, had received the reward of righteousness and of an everlasting priesthood. Luke says: That the Lord touched the ear and healed it (Luke 22). For he never forgets his kindness, and does not allow even his enemies to be wounded. Mystically: teaching that those who contracted a wound of the soul by consenting to his death, if they repent worthily, can merit salvation.
14.48: 14.48 As against a robber. THE SAME. As if to say: It is foolish to seize with swords and clubs one who of his own accord hands himself over to you, and to hunt him by night through a betrayer as though he were hiding, when he teaches daily in the temple. But you gather against me in darkness because your power is in darkness.
14.50: 14.50 Then, etc. THE SAME. What he said is fulfilled, that all would be scandalized, etc., up to and, having to be recalled by God, they learned to give to adversaries.
14.52: 14.52 But he, etc. As Joseph, leaving his cloak behind, escaped naked from the hands of his shameless mistress. And whoever wishes to escape the hands of the wicked, leaving behind in his mind the things that belong to the world, let him flee after Jesus. From them. Whose presence and deeds he detested. Not from the Lord, whose love, even absent in body, he kept fixed in his mind.
14.53: 14.53 The high priest, etc. That is, Caiaphas, who according to John was high priest that year; of whom Josephus writes, in agreement, that he had bought the high priesthood from the Roman emperor without merit of dignity. What wonder, then, if a wicked high priest judges wickedly?
14.54: 14.54 Afar off. BEDE. Because he was close to denial; if he had been close to Christ he would not have denied him; yet in this he is to be admired, that he did not leave the Lord even though he was afraid. That he feared belongs to nature; that he follows belongs to devotion; that he denies belongs to surprise; that he repents belongs to faith. The court. JEROME. The court is the circuit of the world. The servants are demons. The fire is carnal desire, with which he who remains cannot weep for his sins. And he warmed himself. BEDE. There is a fire of charity, of which it is said, etc., up to and soon he set the secrets of his heart ablaze with the coals of love.
14.56: 14.56 False witness. THE SAME. He is false who does not understand what is said in the same sense in which it is said, etc., up to so that he seems to have spoken properly of the Jewish temple.
14.60: 14.60 And rising up, etc. Angry because he found no ground for slander, by the movement of his body he shows the madness of his mind. Answering nothing, etc. He provokes a reply so as to find from any occasion of speech a ground for accusing. But Jesus did not answer, because he foresaw that whatever he answered would be turned into slander. You are the Christ. JEROME. He did not see near at hand the one whom he had awaited from afar, as Isaac, with dim eyes, did not recognize Jacob under his hands, but long after sang of the things to come concerning him.
14.62: 14.62 And you shall see. The priest asks about the Son of God; Jesus answered the Son of man, so that we may understand that the same is Son of God and Son of man, lest we make a quaternity in the Trinity, and there be man in God and God in man. At the right hand of the power. Because he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross; for which cause God also has exalted him, and has given him a name which is above all names (Phil. 2). With the clouds of heaven. JEROME. He ascended in a cloud, he will come with a cloud; that is, he ascended with only his own body which he took from the Virgin, and he will come to judgment with the manifold Church, which is his body and fullness, as Matthew says: And when the Son of man shall come, and all the angels with him, etc.
14.63: 14.63 And the high priest. BEDE. The same rage which had before cast him from his seat, etc., up to as they did when in Lycaonia they were honored as gods. His garments, etc. JEROME. That is, they lost the ephod in which the Jews had their honor, etc., up to yet its chastity remains inviolate until the consummation of the world in those whom the lot of election shall find.
14.64: 14.64 Who all, etc. JEROME. By this guilt of his he would loosen our guilt, etc., up to hence the prophet: What shall I render to the Lord for all the things that he has rendered to me? (Ps. 115).
14.65: 14.65 To cover his face, etc. Not that he may not see their crimes, but, as they once did to Moses, that they may hide from themselves the grace of knowing him. This veil remains to this day upon their heart, which is taken away for those who believe in Christ. Hence at his dying the temple was torn, as it were, and the secrets of the holy of holies laid open. They struck him with the palms of their hands. BEDE. He who was then beaten with blows is even now beaten by the blasphemies of false Christians. He who was consumed with the spittle of unbelievers is now dishonored by the mad reproaches of believers.
14.68: 14.68 But he, etc. Note that he denies Christ who denies that he is his disciple. For the Lord did not say: You will deny that you are my disciple, but: You will deny me. He therefore denied him when he denied that he was his disciple. And he went out, etc. JEROME. Peter, without the Spirit, yielded to the voice of a maidservant, etc., up to and we go outside, outside of what we were.
14.70: 14.70 For you also are a Galilean. BEDE. Galileans and Jerusalemites have the same language, but every province and region has its own manner of speaking, which it is hard to change, etc., up to because the people of Jerusalem and the Galileans pronounced that name differently.
14.72: 14.72 And he remembered. THE SAME. Peter denies by night; at the cock's crow he repents. In the day, he who had denied three times professed three times that he loved. For what, etc., up to he goes out (as the other Evangelists relate), so that, separated from the impious, he may wash away the fault of the denial more freely with tears.
15.1: 15.1 And straightway, etc. There follows: Binding Jesus. It was the custom of the Jews that one whom they had adjudged to death they handed over bound to the judge. And it should be noted that they had not bound him then for the first time, but immediately after seizing him by night in the garden, as John says: And so they led him first to Annas (John 18). JEROME. Samson is here, bound by Delilah. Samson is interpreted, etc., up to and he opens for us who thirst the fountain of perennial life, that is, of his body.
15.2: 15.2 Are you the king of the Jews? When Pilate asks about no crime except whether he is the king of the Jews, the impiety of those is exposed who could not find even a false charge to bring. You say it. He tempers the answer so as to speak the truth, and yet not to yield to slander. And note that he answered Pilate, who gave sentence unwillingly, in some part; but to the priests and princes he would not answer, and judged them unworthy of his speech.
15.4: 15.4 See, etc. A pagan condemns Jesus, but refers the cause to the people of the Jews. See of how many things, etc.
15.11: 15.11 That he should rather release Barabbas. BEDA. Their petition clings to the Jews to this day, which they obtained with all their effort. For, an option having been given them, they chose a robber in place of Jesus, a murderer in place of the Savior. Rightly, then, they lost salvation and life, and so far subjected themselves to robberies and seditions that they lost kingdom and country, and never recovered freedom of body and soul.
15.14: 15.14 But Pilate. Pilate gave many occasions for freeing the Savior: first, comparing a robber with the just man; then asking: What will you then that I do with the king of the Jews? And when they answered: Let him be crucified, he did not at once yield, but according to the suggestion of his wife, who had sent word to him (as Matthew says): Have nothing to do with that just man (Matt. 27), he answered and said: Why, what evil has he done? By saying this he acquitted Jesus. But they the more, etc. David: Many dogs have encompassed me (Ps. 21), etc. Isaias: I looked that he should do judgment, and behold iniquity; and justice, and behold a cry (Isa. 5). Jeremias: My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it has cried out against me (Jer. 12).
15.15: 15.15 Barabbas, and delivered, etc. JEROME. These are the two goats: one, apopompaeus, that is, the scapegoat, with the sin of the people is sent away released into the desert of hell. The other is slain like a lamb for the sins of those absolved. The Lord's portion is always sacrificed; the devil's portion, who is their master, is cast headlong, unrestrained, into Tartarus. Jesus with scourges. That he might free us from scourges; whence: The scourge shall not come near your tabernacle (Ps. 90), whereas before it was said: Many are the scourges of the sinner (Ps. 31). BEDA. Jesus scourged. He was scourged by Pilate himself, whence John: Pilate took Jesus and scourged him; and afterwards he added: And the soldiers platting a crown of thorns (John 19), etc. And he gave him to the soldiers to mock. He did this so that, sated with his sufferings and insults, they might not thirst beyond his death.
15.17: 15.17 And they clothe. BEDA. Matthew says thus: And stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak about him (Marc. 27). Which is the same thing. For it was given in place of the royal purple, etc., up to he is clothed in purple or scarlet when he glories in the triumph of the glorious martyrs.
15.19: 15.19 And they struck, etc. The head of Christ is God. They therefore strike the head of Christ who deny that he is God. And those who defend their error by the authority of Scripture (because writing is usually done with a reed) strike his head, as it were, with a reed. They spit in his face who reject the presence of his grace with execrable words conceived from the inner madness of a blind mind, and deny that he came in the flesh. Bowing the knee they adored him. As if he had falsely called himself God. But today (which is a graver madness) some adore him with sure faith as true God, but by perverse acts soon despise his words as fables, and put the promises of his kingdom after temporal enticements. And they lead him out. JEROME. Here Abel is led out into the field by his brother to be killed. Here Isaac is present, etc., up to here Jonas is present, cast out of the wood of the ship into the sea and into the belly of the whale for three days.
15.20: 15.20 To crucify him. JEROME. What is the very shape of the cross but the form of the four-cornered world? The east shines forth from its power, the right hand holds the north, the south stands at the left, the west is made firm beneath the feet. Hence the Apostle: That we may know what is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth (Eph. 3). Birds fly to the heavens in the form of a cross, man prays, and swims in the form of a cross, the ship is driven across the seas by a yard-arm made like a cross. The letter Tau shows the sign of salvation and of the cross.
15.21: 15.21 And they compelled. BEDA. The Lord himself first carried his cross, as John says: Afterwards this Simon, of whom the others also speak, and this in a fitting order of the mystery. For Christ suffered for us, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps (John 19; 1 Pet. 2). JEROME. Simon, who carries the cross under compulsion, is he who labors for human praise. Men compel him to this labor, whom neither fear nor love of God compels. The father of Alexander. This Simon appears to have been of great reputation, since his sons also are designated by name as known to all. JEROME. Some are commemorated through the merits of their fathers, others through the merits of their sons. But this Simon, etc., up to whence, through Jeremiah, it is said to Judea: The Lord called your name a fruitful olive tree, fair, beautiful.
15.22: 15.22 The place of Calvary. JEROME. The Jews hand down that in this place on the mountain a ram was sacrificed in place of Isaac (Gen. 22), so that there Christ might be made bald, that is, separated from his flesh, namely carnal Judea. BEDE. Outside the gate the heads of the condemned were cut off, and the places of the beheaded are called Calvaries. Therefore the Lord was crucified there, that where the field of the condemned was, there the banners of the martyrs might be raised. And since the curse of the cross was made for us, and he was scourged and crucified for the salvation of all, he willed to be crucified as a criminal among criminals.
15.23: 15.23 And they gave. BEDA. Matthew says, mingled with gall (Matt. 27), which is the same thing. For he put gall for bitterness. Wine with myrrh is most bitter; though it may be that they made the wine most bitter with both gall and myrrh. JEROME. And they gave, etc. By this vinegar the deadly juice of the fruit is wiped away. And he took it not. That for which he suffers. Whence of him: What I took not away, I then restored (Ps. 68). And he took it not. Matthew: And when he had tasted, he would not drink. Matthew indicates that he tasted the bitterness of death for us, but on the third day he rose again.
15.24: 15.24 And crucifying him with. JEROME. Here salvation is fixed on the wood. First death was fixed on the wood. The first tree was of the knowledge of good and evil; the second is for us the tree of good alone and of life. The stretching out of the first hand to the tree seized death; the stretching out of the second found the life that had perished. By this wood we are borne across the stormy sea to the land of the living. His garments. BEDA. Christ's garment divided in four parts according to the number of the soldiers signifies the Church, distributed equally, that is, harmoniously, over the four parts of the world. JEROME. The garments of the Lord are the commandments with which his body, which is the Church, is covered, because they are divided among the soldiers of the nations so that there are four orders though there is one faith, that is, the married, the widowed, the prelates, the separated. They cast lots for the undivided tunic, which is peace and truth in all, after the manner of a royal robe or ring. Casting lots. THE SAME. Upon the tunic, namely that which was seamless. Here the lot, etc., up to and the lot comes or falls by the judgment of God alone.
15.25: 15.25 And it was the third hour. JEROME. This is Mark's peculiarity, for at the sixth hour darkness covered the earth, so that no one could move his head. For from the thirtieth, etc., up to who are rather to be said to have crucified him, though they try to dissemble it, than the soldiers who, according to their duty, obeyed their commander.
15.26: 15.26 And the inscription. BEDA. The inscription shows that not even by killing him could they bring it about that he should not be their king; whence: But I am appointed king by him, etc. Well is he at once king and priest, since he offered to the Father the choice victim of his flesh on the altar of the cross, and displayed the dignity of a king in the inscription, to make known to all that through the gibbet of the cross he did not lose, but confirmed his dominion.
15.27: 15.27 And with him they crucify. BEDA. As the Apostle says: Our old man is crucified together with him, that the body of sin may be destroyed, to the end that we may serve sin no longer. So long, then, as they do our works so that the body of sin may be made void, so long, etc., up to whence the Apostle: That being rooted and founded in charity, you may be able to comprehend, with all the saints, what is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth (Eph. 3). Two robbers. THE SAME. The robbers who were crucified with the Lord signify those who undergo, by faith and confession of Christ, or by the struggle of their martyrdom, or by any strict continence. And those who do this for eternal glory are signified by the merit and faith of the right-hand robber. But he who does it for human glory or any less worthy intention imitates the mind and acts of the left-hand robber. JEROME. Truth, reckoned among the wicked, leaves one on the left, takes the other on the right; so will he do on the day of judgment: from a like crime they receive unlike paths. One goes before Peter into paradise, the other Judas into hell. A short confession gains a long life, and a blasphemy, once ended, is punished with eternal penalty. This is the foal of Judah bound to the vine, that is, the cloak dyed in the blood of the grape; here the kids tear the vineyard.
15.29: 15.29 Wagging their heads. JEROME. The death of the wicked is sent forth when the bonds of hell are stirred up as far as the neck, which is the neck of the human race.
15.31: 15.31 Others he saved. JEROME. Even unwillingly they confess that he saved others, and they condemn themselves by their own sentence, because he saved others, and could have saved himself if he wished.
15.32: 15.32 Let him come down now. It is more to rise from the sepulchre, and yet they did not believe. They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together (Ps. 13). And they that were crucified with him. BEDA. According to Luke (Luke 23), one robber blasphemed, saying: If you are the Christ, save yourself and us. The other, etc., up to who seek heavenly things, they arrive at them without doubt, Christ mediating and showing mercy.
15.33: 15.33 And when the sixth hour was come. BEDA. It should be noted that he was crucified at the sixth hour, that is, when the sun was about to depart from the center of the world, and at dawn, at sunrise, he rose, etc., up to and at the hour at which the first Adam by sinning brought death into the world, at that same hour the second Adam by dying would destroy death. Darkness. JEROME. Here Noe is present, drunken and naked, covered with the drunken cloak of heaven and earth, and mocked by a man; here blood dripped from the tree.
15.35: 15.35 And some, etc. Not all. Perhaps the Roman soldiers, not understanding the property of the Hebrew speech, from the word Eloi thought that Elias was being called by him. Or the Jews, perverting the Lord's words in their usual manner, defamed him with weakness, as if he called on Elias for help.
15.36: 15.36 And running, etc. BEDA. John says more fully: After this, Jesus knowing, etc. As if to say: You have done this less; give what you are. For there were, etc., up to concerning which: The Lord planted the vineyard of Soreth; and how are you turned into bitterness, O strange vine; and I looked that you should bring forth grapes, and you have brought forth thorns (Isa. 5).
15.37: 15.37 And Jesus, etc. BEDA. Luke reveals what he said: Father, into your hands I commend my spirit; and saying this he gave up the ghost (Luke 23). But what John says: When he had received the vinegar, he said: It is consummated; and bowing his head he gave up the ghost (John 19). Between his saying: It is consummated, and that: bowing his head he gave up the ghost, that great voice was uttered, which John passes over in silence, and the others record: Into your hands, etc. JEROME. For when the flesh was weakened, the divine power straightway prevailed, which says: Open to me the gates of justice (Ps. 117), etc. But we, who are of the earth, die with no voice, or with one; for he who came down from heaven expired with a raised voice.
15.38: 15.38 And the veil of the temple. So that the ark of the testament and all the sacraments of the law which were covered might appear, and pass over to the Gentiles. Before it was said: In Judea God is known, in Israel his name is great (Ps. 75); but now: Be exalted above the heavens, O God (ibid. 56), and in all, etc.; and in the Gospel before: Go not into the way of the Gentiles (Matt. 10); and after the passion: Go, and teach all nations (ibid. 28).
15.39: 15.39 And the centurion seeing, etc. It is shown why the centurion wondered: because he saw that he had so expired, that is, had sent forth his spirit. For no one has power to send forth his spirit except the Creator of souls. Truly, etc. JEROME. Note that the centurion before the cross, in the very scandal of the passion, confesses him truly the Son of God; and Arius, etc., up to and the Synagogue being silent, he affirms truly the Son of God.
15.40: 15.40 And there were. THE SAME. As the female sex is not excluded from salvation through the Virgin Mary, so it is not barred from the mystery of the cross, of knowledge, and of resurrection through the widow Mary Magdalene and the other mothers. Of James the less and of Joseph. BEDA. He calls James the less James the son of Alphaeus, who is also the brother of the Lord, because he was the son of Mary, the Lord's mother's sister. Of whom John: Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother (John 19), etc. He seems to say Cleophas's from the father or from kinship.
15.42: 15.42 And when evening was now come, etc. THE SAME. Parasceve in Greek, preparation in Latin. By this name the Jews dwelling among the Greeks called the sixth day of the sabbath, because on it they prepared what was necessary for the sabbath, according to what, etc., up to until, the eighth age coming, the bodies themselves, glorified by the resurrection, together with the souls receive the incorruption of the eternal inheritance.
15.43: 15.43 Joseph came. JEROME. Joseph came in the evening of the parasceve from Arimathea, which is interpreted taking down, to take down the body of Christ, etc., up to the elect, who are the stars of the sea, looking on from afar, when, if it can be, even the elect will be scandalized.
15.46: 15.46 And Joseph, etc. BEDA. From the simple burial of the Lord the ambition of the rich is condemned, who neither in tombs, etc., up to celebrates with earthly linen, as the body of the Lord was buried in a clean shroud; so it was decreed by Pope Sylvester. Which was hewn out. BEDA. It is said that the Lord's monument was a round house cut out of the underlying rock, of such height that a man standing upright could scarcely touch the top with his hand stretched out. And it has an entrance, etc., up to and the color of the monument and of the sepulchre is said to be a mixture of white and red.
15.47: 15.47 And Mary, etc. THE SAME. Luke says: And all his acquaintance stood afar off, and the women that had followed him (Luke 23). But the others returning to their homes after his body was laid down, the women alone, etc., up to and if perhaps they may be able to imitate with pious curiosity, in what order his passion is to be embraced, they consider carefully.
16.1: 16.1 And when the sabbath was past. BEDA. Luke says that returning from the monument they prepared spices and ointments, and on the sabbath they rested, because it was commanded that the silence of the sabbath, etc., up to with face enlightened, the darkness of vices being shaken off, to offer to the Lord the fragrance of good works and the sweetness of prayers. JEROME. Now with fragrant spices they run with the bride and the young maidens; afterwards we sprinkle the book, that is, the couch, etc., up to and the Lord rising in it with triumph and saying: This is the day which the Lord has made, etc. (Ps. 117).
16.2: 16.2 And very early. JEROME. What another calls dawn. The dawn is between the darkness of night and the brightness of day, in which salvation came to be declared in the Church after the manner of the sun, which as it rises sends before it a rosy dawn, so that so great a splendor may be seen by eyes made ready, when the time of the Lord's resurrection shone forth, that then the whole Church might sing the praises of Christ of the holy women, when he gave life and poured in the light of belief.
16.3: 16.3 And they said one to another. JEROME. The eagles are gathered together to the body; the martyrs and apostles see the stone rolled back, which is the law of death, as if to say: Where, O death, is your sting? (1 Cor. 15).
16.4: 16.4 The stone rolled back. BEDA. How the stone was rolled back by an angel, Matthew tells. Allegorically, however, the rolling back of the stone signifies the resurrection of the sacraments of Christ, which were covered by the veil of the letter of the law. For the law was written on stone; its covering being taken away, the glory of the resurrection was shown, and the abolition of the old death, and the everlasting life to be hoped for by us began to be preached throughout the whole world.
16.5: 16.5 A young man. JEROME. Not an old man, not an infant, but one pleasant in age, as it is said: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth (Eccles. 11), which is not true here while mingled with old age. BEDA. The women who came with spices see angels, because those minds behold the heavenly citizens which come to God with virtues through holy desires. Sitting on the right side. BEDA. On the southern side of the place where he had been laid, etc., up to entering the monument they found two angels standing there. GREGORY. By the left is meant the present life, by the right eternal life, etc., up to and, restoring the number of the angels, he repaired the losses of the heavenly country.
16.6: 16.6 Be not affrighted. GREGORY. As if to say: Let those be afraid who do not love the coming of the Lord or of the heavenly citizens, who, pressed down by vices, despair of their company. But you, why do you fear, who see your fellow citizens? Whence Matthew, describing the angel's appearing, says: His countenance was as lightning, and his raiment as snow (Matt. 28). Jesus. Savior. But because many were called by this name not in substance but in title, he determines by the place, the Nazarene, and adds the cause: Who was crucified. And he adds: He is risen, he is not here. By the presence of the flesh; yet he is nowhere absent by the presence of majesty. Behold the place. Mortality is shown to mortals for the due giving of thanks, that we may understand what we are and have been, and know what we shall be.
16.7: 16.7 And Peter. BEDA. Peter is called by name, lest he despair because of his denial. For unless, etc., up to that he who was to be the shepherd of the Church might learn in his own fault how he ought to have mercy on others. And Peter. JEROME. He who shows himself unworthy of discipleship when he denies his master three times. But past sins do not harm when they do not please. He goes before you. Rightly is it said of our Redeemer: for Galilee is interpreted passing over. For he had already passed over from passion to resurrection, from death to life, from punishment to glory. And rightly after the resurrection he is seen in Galilee by the disciples, because we shall see the glory of his resurrection afterwards with joy, if only we pass over from vices to the height of virtues. He, then, who is announced in the sepulchre is shown in the passing over; and he who is recognized in the mortification of the flesh is seen in the passing over of the mind. BEDA. Note that Mark says: He goes before you into Galilee, etc. Yet he did not report that he was seen there. But Matthew, etc., up to as he will be known in that eternity, to which he will also lead us on account of the form of a servant, that being free we may contemplate the form of the Lord.
16.8: 16.8 They fled. JEROME. Of the future life it is said: Sorrow and mourning shall flee away. The women imitate before the resurrection of all what they do after, that is, what they are about to do: they flee death and terror. And to no man. JEROME. Because only those see the mystery of the resurrection who have deserved it, whence, according to John: Peter, rising up, ran to the sepulchre, to see what he had heard.
16.9: 16.9 Now rising. He rose in the morning, was buried in the evening, to fulfill this: In the evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness (Ps. 29). Buried, then, on the sixth day of the sabbath, which is called parasceve, about evening, the following night and the day of the sabbath, since he was laid in the monument the following night, on the third day, that is, early on the first day of the sabbath, he rose. And rightly he lay one day and two nights in the sepulchre, because he joined the light of his single death to the darkness of our double death. For in the death of soul and spirit we were held; whence he brought to us his own death, that is, of the flesh, and loosed our two: he brought his single to our double, and by dying took away our double. He appeared first to Mary Magdalene. He is shown first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils: because harlots and publicans go before the Synagogue into the kingdom of God, as the robber went before the apostles. The apostles weep and mourn, because they have not yet seen, but they will soon be consoled. BEDA. In the beginning the woman was the author of the fault to the man, the man the executor of the error, etc., up to that she might herself announce the resurrection to the evangelists and apostles themselves.
16.11: 16.11 And they hearing. BEDA. That the disciples were slow to believe the resurrection is not so much their weakness as our strength; for to those who doubted the resurrection was shown by many proofs, by which we also are more firmly established.
16.12: 16.12 Two of them. BEDA. Luke says this more openly (Luke 24): Their eyes, etc. Afterwards they knew him in the breaking of bread. And as Luke says: Rising up the same hour, they returned to Jerusalem, etc. Walking. JEROME. Faith labors here, practicing the active life, there the contemplative, etc., up to forgetful of his flesh, he asks in this life what we hope for after it in the future.
16.14: 16.14 Last of all, etc. BEDA. On the fortieth day, when he was about to depart from them into heaven, this above all to them, etc., up to: Going into the whole world, preach the Gospel. Hardness of heart, etc. JEROME. That a heart of flesh full of charity may succeed; hence the companies of martyrs willingly seek the death of this world, because they know that through a temporal destruction they will live forever.
16.15: 16.15 To every creature. To every nation of the Gentiles. For before it had been said: Go not into the way of the Gentiles (Matt. 10); namely, that the preaching of the apostles, first repelled by Judea, might then become a help to the Gentiles. JEROME. To every kind of human being, which has something in common with every creature: with angels, cattle, trees, stones, fire and water, hot and cold, moist and dry, because man is called the lesser world.
16.16: 16.16 He that believes, etc. Through others little children believe, as from others they drew the sins which are remitted to them in baptism.
16.17: 16.17 And these signs, etc. Do we not believe if we do not work signs? But these were necessary in the beginning, that faith might be nourished by miracles, but with the faith of the Church now confirmed they are not necessary. They shall cast out devils, etc. This the Church does today spiritually, when through the grace of exorcism she lays her hand on believers and drives out evil spirits. They shall speak with new tongues. This is done when the faithful leave behind the worldly words of their old life, and sound forth holy mysteries, and extol the praises and power of God as much as they can.
16.18: 16.18 If they drink any deadly thing, etc. When they hear pestilent persuasions and do not carry them as far as action, so that it does not harm them if they drink a deadly thing. They shall lay hands upon the sick, etc. When they strengthen their neighbors, confirmed in good work, by the example of good action, they lay hands upon the sick, and they shall recover. These miracles are as much greater as they are spiritual; for by this souls are raised, not bodies.
16.19: 16.19 Into heaven. AUGUSTINE. Note that sometimes he says heavens in the plural and sometimes heaven in the singular, etc., up to where the belief of the faithful is taught more by deeds than by words. And sits on the right hand. BEDE. And even now judging all things, at the end he will come as Judge of all. But Stephen saw him standing, because in the struggle he had him as helper.
16.20: 16.20 But they, etc. BEDA. Note that the later Mark began his Gospel, the more, etc., up to by which the apostles sowed the same word of the Gospel throughout the whole world.
